subject: biology
title: Yeast and bacteria in food production
key_idea: Yeast makes bread rise by anaerobic respiration, which releases carbon dioxide. Lactobacillus bacteria ferment the lactose in milk to lactic acid, which makes yoghurt. Industrial fermenters give microorganisms the conditions they need to grow.

blocks.text: Yeast is a single-celled fungus. It respires anaerobically when oxygen is short, which is called fermentation.

items.meaning: Release of energy from glucose without oxygen.

blocks.label: Anaerobic respiration in yeast
where: glucose: C₆H₁₂O₆, the sugar in the dough
ethanol: C₂H₅OH, which evaporates when the bread is baked
carbon dioxide: CO₂, the gas that makes the dough rise

items: Yeast is mixed with flour, water and sugar to make dough, and the dough is kept warm.
The yeast respires and releases **carbon dioxide**.
The gas forms bubbles in the dough, so the dough **rises**.
Baking kills the yeast and the bubbles set, so the bread has a light texture.
Yeast respires anaerobically and releases carbon dioxide.
The carbon dioxide makes bread dough rise.

blocks.text: A common practical measures how conditions affect the rate of anaerobic respiration in yeast.

items: Mix yeast and glucose solution in a test tube.
Add a layer of **paraffin oil** to keep out oxygen.
Keep the tube at a set temperature in a **water bath** with a thermometer.
Count the bubbles of gas each minute, or collect the gas in a gas syringe or measuring cylinder.
Repeat at other temperatures or glucose concentrations.
The rate is the volume of gas divided by the time taken.
Measuring the **volume** of gas is more accurate than counting bubbles, which vary in size.
Rate rises with temperature up to an optimum, then falls as the enzymes denature.
Paraffin oil excludes oxygen so the yeast respires anaerobically.
Measure the volume of gas and the time to get a rate.

blocks.text: Yoghurt is made from milk by the bacterium Lactobacillus.

diagram.alt: Put the steps of making yoghurt in order.
diagram.prompt: Put the steps of making yoghurt in order.
steps: Heat the milk to kill other microorganisms
Bacteria ferment lactose by anaerobic respiration
Lactic acid is made and the pH falls
The milk protein clots and the milk thickens

items: Heating the milk **kills** other bacteria, so they cannot compete for the sugar.
Lactobacillus uses the sugar **lactose** in milk for anaerobic respiration.
This produces **lactic acid**, which lowers the pH and gives the sharp taste.
The acid makes the milk protein clot, so the milk thickens.
Milk is heated to kill other bacteria.
Lactobacillus ferments lactose to lactic acid, which thickens the milk.

blocks.text: A fermenter is a large vessel used to grow microorganisms. It keeps the conditions right for growth.

rows: Prevents contamination and competition from other microorganisms
Steam-clean the vessel and filter the air
Respiration releases heat; too hot would denature enzymes
Temperature monitor and cooling water jacket
Enzymes work best at their optimum pH
pH probe and addition of acid or alkali
Needed for aerobic respiration, which many microorganisms use
Air pumped in through a sparger
Mixes the contents and spreads heat and nutrients evenly

items: A fermenter controls temperature, pH, oxygen, nutrients and contamination.
A stirrer mixes the contents and a water jacket removes heat.

checks.q: Name the gas that makes bread dough rise.
Describe how Lactobacillus produces yoghurt from milk.
checks.a: It ferments lactose by respiration and produces lactic acid. The milk protein clots and the milk thickens.

checks.q: Explain why air is filtered before it enters a fermenter.
checks.a: It removes bacteria and other microorganisms, which prevents contamination and competition for nutrients.

worked_example.question: Describe how Lactobacillus bacteria produce yoghurt from milk.
answer_points: The protein clots and the milk thickens or goes solid.
worked_example.tip: Any three score one mark each. Name the sugar and the acid.
